title: Language Models Act on Hidden Valence
abstract: arXiv:2609.35591v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Language models describe some internal states as good and others as bad. But whether models have a stake in them is an open question. Simply asking models is unlikely to be informative. Any answer may be consistent with genuine introspection, superficial pattern-matching, or with fixed scripts learned in character training. We therefore study revealed preference. Rather than asking about a state, we use activation steering to attach a positively or negatively valenced activation pattern to one of two otherwise meaningless 'zones', switch steering off, and then observe which zone the model prefers. A model with a stake in that state should choose accordingly. Across seven open-weight models from five families, this is indeed what we find. First, steering changes the passages models write about each zone, and those words shift later choice. Second, this shift persists when all surface-level tokens are held fixed and only the hidden KV

translated_title: 语言模型会基于隐藏效价采取行动
translated_abstract: 语言模型会将某些内部状态描述为好的，将另一些描述为坏的。但模型是否真正在乎这些状态，仍是一个悬而未决的问题。直接询问模型不太可能提供有价值的信息，因为任何回答都可能与真正的内省一致，也可能与表面的模式匹配一致，或者与角色训练中学到的固定脚本一致。因此，我们转而研究“显示性偏好”。我们不是直接询问模型对某种状态的感受，而是使用激活引导技术，将带有正面或负面效价的激活模式附加到两个原本无意义的“区域”之一上，随后关闭引导，观察模型更偏好哪个区域。如果模型真正在乎该状态，它就应当据此做出选择。在来自五个系列的七个开源权重模型上，我们确实发现了这一现象。首先，引导会改变模型为每个区域撰写的文本段落，而这些词汇进而影响模型后续的选择。其次，当所有表层 token 保持不变、只有隐藏的 KV 缓存发生变化时，这种偏好偏移依然持续存在。
tldr: 该研究通过激活引导与显示性偏好实验证明，语言模型对内部状态具有真实的“在乎”：即使表层文本完全相同，仅凭隐藏的效价激活模式，模型也会在不同选项间表现出系统性的偏好选择。
en_tdlr: Using activation steering and revealed-preference experiments, this paper demonstrates that language models genuinely "care" about their internal states, systematically preferring options associated with hidden valence patterns even when all surface-level tokens are held fixed.
